evidence.note: NO WEBGL CONTEXT AT ALL on a GPU-less Linux host running HEADED, which is upstream of every GPU value this fork serves and was hidden by measuring headless. Measured by CollectorLinux on a real headless server under Xvfb: canvas.getContext("webgl") returns null, gpu/command_buffer/service/context_group.cc reports ContextResult::kFatalFailure "WebGL1 blocklisted", chrome://gpu reports WebGL disabled via blocklist, and glxinfo -B reports llvmpipe with Accelerated: no. MECHANISM, read out of ui/gl/gl_features.cc: features::IsSwiftShaderAllowed() is IsSwiftShaderAllowedByCommandLine() OR IsSwiftShaderAllowedByFeature(); the first is true only for --enable-unsafe-swiftshader or --use-angle=swiftshader[-for-webgl], and the second is kAllowSwiftShaderFallback, which upstream left FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT after deprecating the implicit fallback from Chrome 130 and removing it on Linux and macOS from Chrome 139. With Mesa llvmpipe the only driver, the blocklist disables WebGL and nothing may replace it. --headless=new enables the fallback for itself, which is why every earlier measurement saw a working SwiftShader context. CollectorLinux proved the opt-in is the whole difference: bare headed gives a null context and a rejected capture, --enable-unsafe-swiftshader gives 44 of 44 probes. A null context is a stronger tell than any renderer string, because effectively no real desktop browser lacks WebGL. Patch 0108 flips kAllowSwiftShaderFallback to enabled by default -- a feature rather than an appended switch, because it needs no propagation to the GPU process, leaves no argv footprint, and cannot be keyed on patch 0091's detection, which is one-way and reports a hardware backend on the reference host because /dev/dri/renderD128 is present with no usable driver behind it. It ALLOWS rather than forces the fallback. 0108 also regates the decoder's SwiftShader deprecation console message on features::IsSwiftShaderAllowed() instead of the raw switch, because that message goes to the page's console and would otherwise announce software WebGL on every GPU-less launch. No hole on Windows: IsAnySoftwareGLAllowed() ORs IsWARPAllowed() and kAllowD3D11WarpFallback is enabled by default. macOS has the same hole and the same fix. Needs V3 on a GPU-less Linux host to close.
evidence.source: CollectorLinux measurement on a headless Linux server under Xvfb, headed, plus ui/gl/gl_features.cc read at this revision

notes: Line 4202 at this revision; 4214 on main. Symbol is authoritative, line is advisory. Bound on the per-field override (patch 0085, unbuilt): --fingerprint-gpu-renderer and --fingerprint-gpu-vendor act only as a RESTRICTION on the gpu_identity draw within the resolved anchor — the chosen option is still a measured catalogue member, WebGPU still comes from that member, and a name the resolved anchor never measured is refused with the servable identities listed. An override cannot widen the legal identity set beyond the measured pairs. Evidence by symbol: base/apostate/compose.cc NarrowToNamedIdentity, IdentityOfOption, Compose. CROSS-SEED LINKING PROPERTY, which holds under BOTH readings of the measurement above and is the consequence worth acting on: because this value is constant on a host while other axes rotate per seed, it is a LINKING IDENTIFIER across identities. Two personas drawn from two different --fingerprint seeds on the same machine present the same GPU, so a detector does not need to recognise an M4 Max — it only needs to notice that two identities it should not be able to connect share one. If the pinning is deliberate, the design has that property and it must be DOCUMENTED rather than discovered; if the axis is composed but not reaching the emitter, this is a wiring defect and a four-target build will not fix an emitter that is not wired. Either way the row stays open and the ruling is not this row's to make. RULING: satisfy the linking property by giving the axis real per-seed entropy, which the current tree does — 29 renderer strings in the generated catalogue, twelve Apple from M1 through M4 Max, each validated byte-for-byte against its anchor's measured template. The cause was never pinning: it was an anchor with one measured member, and the binary said so in --fingerprint-explain while nothing read it. Two things remain true and are recorded on coh.per-seed-entropy-across-axes rather than here: a widened table proves nothing about selection, so the edge is UNVERIFIED until an unpinned-launch run on the built binary shows the renderer rotating and stable under a pinned seed; and the pool is PER ANCHOR, so a host whose backend maps to a thinly measured anchor still has little cross-seed entropy, which --fingerprint-explain's member count is the honest way to surface.

notes: Two emission sites in two processes, exactly the shape that makes Device-Memory dangerous: content/browser/client_hints/client_hints.cc:674 adds this header to NAVIGATION requests in the browser, third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_fetch_context.cc:641 adds it to SUBRESOURCE requests in the renderer. Serialisation goes through blink::UserAgentMetadata::SerializeBrandVersionList (user_agent_metadata.cc:35), RFC 8941 structured headers — which is why the browser and renderer sites produce byte-identical values and why a hand-assembled string would not.

evidence.note: the opt-in readback policy is applied to the caller's ImageData after the clean read, so the canvas's backing store and every snapshot taken from it stay exactly as rendered; with --fingerprint-noise absent the call is a no-op and the bytes are stock

notes: A real render, not a stored value, so A1 forbids intercepting the readback, and by default nothing perturbs it. Patch 0120 adds one exception behind --fingerprint-noise, off unless asked for: a profile-seeded, content-keyed step of one unit of what the canvas holds, on the colour channels, applied at each page-visible output, with flat neighbourhoods and alpha left alone so a solid fill stays byte-exact. The step is keyed on the colour rather than on the bytes: measured against the built binary, keying on memory made getImageData (straight RGBA8) and an encoded snapshot (premultiplied BGRA) of one canvas disagree -- 687 pixels moved against 704, only 49 of the 749 differing pixels a channel swap -- so the kernel canonicalises to straight alpha in logical RGBA order, steps there, and writes back through the store's own convention. On a translucent pixel the straight-alpha step is the nearest value the premultiplied store can hold (two at half alpha, more as alpha falls) so that every route reports the same number; the composited change stays one. It is deterministic per profile, so A3 still holds; what it trades is this row's own coherence bar, and docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 5 records that. Default behaviour is unchanged. The inputs are, in descending order of effect: the ANGLE backend and driver (see gpu.angle-backend), the raster mode (GPU vs CPU, ShouldAccelerate), the two canvas antialiasing switches, text rasterisation settings, and the installed font set. Of those, everything except the driver is configurable per profile with existing Chromium mechanisms. Determinism is measured, not assumed: the same bytes across two page loads. Note the raster mode can change WITHIN a session - the second getImageData on a canvas without willReadFrequently disables acceleration (kFallbackToCPUAfterReadbacks = 2) - so a probe that reads the same canvas twice may be comparing a GPU render to a CPU one in stock Chrome too; that needs a T0 measurement before we treat any difference as our own bug. Patch 0122 makes the text-rasterisation settings in that list follow the persona instead of the host: gfx::GetFontRenderParams returns the profile's tuple in every process, so Skia's text contrast and gamma, the LCD pixel geometry, subpixel positioning, embedded bitmaps and the SkFont edging the macOS CoreText path sets are the claimed machine's. Measured before it, on this Mac a Windows persona and a macOS persona produced the same digest df91c47fa322e806 for a canvas drawn in three families whose advances both resolve identically -- the host's rasterisation under both names. The two changes compose in one order: 0122 moves which pixels the rasteriser produces, 0120 conditionally moves the bytes handed to the page after that.

notes: THE ESCALATION. What determines the rendered bytes of canvas.2d and webgl.readpixels, in descending order of effect. (1) The ANGLE backend. It fixes the shader translator output, the rasterisation rules, and the whole limit/precision/extension table. Selectable at runtime with --use-angle, but bounded by the host OS: Metal exists only on Apple, D3D11 only on Windows. (2) The GPU driver underneath ANGLE. Not configurable. This is the irreducible residue. (3) The driver-bug workaround set - 142 workarounds, 253 list entries, all keyed on GPUInfo fields we are already spoofing, each forceable by switch. This is Chromium's own mechanism for making rendering differ deterministically per device, and it is already shipping. (4) MSAA sample count and resolve mode (webgl.antialias-samples). (5) Canvas 2D raster mode, GPU or CPU, via --disable-accelerated-2d-canvas and the readback fallback. (6) --disable-2d-canvas-antialiasing and --disable-2d-canvas-clip-antialiasing. (7) Text rasterisation: SkFont edging, hinting and subpixel positioning, plus the eight RendererPreferences font-render-params fields on Linux. (8) The installed font set (owned by subsystem 7). (9) The image encoder, which is constant. RECOMMENDATION. Items 3 to 7 are all existing, deterministic, per-process configuration and should be driven from the profile; none requires per-pixel interference and none violates A3. Item 1 is the hard constraint and it forces a structural decision: profiles must be partitioned by OS and ANGLE backend, and a profile may only be loaded on a host that can provide its backend. A macOS/Metal profile on a Linux host is not a patching problem, it is an impossible claim - webgpu.preferred-canvas-format alone gives it away in one property read before any render is compared. The concrete first step is to set GPUInfo to the profile's device before gpu::ComputeGpuFeatureInfo runs, so that the blocklist, the workaround set, the disabled-extension set and the MSAA count all follow the claimed device using Chromium's own tables rather than the host's hardware. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED, and what would settle it: how large the residual difference is between two GPUs on the same OS and backend. The ANGLE caps table says the reported limits do not differ at all; it says nothing about the pixels. We need two T0 captures on the same OS and ANGLE backend but different GPU models - say an M1 MacBook and this M4 Max - and a diff of probes['canvas.2d'].pixels_sha256 and probes['webgl1'].pixels_sha256. If they match, the backend partition is sufficient and this row closes as a configuration problem. If they differ, we must know by how many pixels and where, because that number is the honest ceiling on GPU-model portability and it belongs in the corpus documentation rather than being discovered by a detector. Explicitly rejected: per-call noise (A3, and coh.render-determinism records that stock Chrome is byte-identical across loads), readback interception (A1), and corpus replay of pixels, which cannot work because a detector chooses the drawing operations. Stays open at V0. Surface measured pre-patch, patch behaviour unbuilt: on this Mac the renderer resolves to ANGLE/Metal with WebGPU adapter apple/metal-3 in every default configuration, and under --use-angle=swiftshader to the SwiftShader string with requestAdapter() returning null. V1, exception now discharged: host_capability.cc, compose.cc, explain.cc AND host_capability_unittest.cc all compile against the pinned build dir, so the two new TESTs are real code rather than text in a patch. Compile only; the row still has no build and no run.

evidence.note: NO WEBGL CONTEXT AT ALL on a GPU-less Linux host running HEADED, which is upstream of every GPU value this fork serves and was hidden by measuring headless. Measured by CollectorLinux on a real headless server under Xvfb: canvas.getContext("webgl") returns null, gpu/command_buffer/service/context_group.cc reports ContextResult::kFatalFailure "WebGL1 blocklisted", chrome://gpu reports WebGL disabled via blocklist, and glxinfo -B reports llvmpipe with Accelerated: no. MECHANISM, read out of ui/gl/gl_features.cc: features::IsSwiftShaderAllowed() is IsSwiftShaderAllowedByCommandLine() OR IsSwiftShaderAllowedByFeature(); the first is true only for --enable-unsafe-swiftshader or --use-angle=swiftshader[-for-webgl], and the second is kAllowSwiftShaderFallback, which upstream left FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT after deprecating the implicit fallback from Chrome 130 and removing it on Linux and macOS from Chrome 139. With Mesa llvmpipe the only driver, the blocklist disables WebGL and nothing may replace it. --headless=new enables the fallback for itself, which is why every earlier measurement saw a working SwiftShader context. CollectorLinux proved the opt-in is the whole difference: bare headed gives a null context and a rejected capture, --enable-unsafe-swiftshader gives 44 of 44 probes. A null context is a stronger tell than any renderer string, because effectively no real desktop browser lacks WebGL. Patch 0108 flips kAllowSwiftShaderFallback to enabled by default -- a feature rather than an appended switch, because it needs no propagation to the GPU process, leaves no argv footprint, and cannot be keyed on patch 0091's detection, which is one-way and reports a hardware backend on the reference host because /dev/dri/renderD128 is present with no usable driver behind it. It ALLOWS rather than forces the fallback. 0108 also regates the decoder's SwiftShader deprecation console message on features::IsSwiftShaderAllowed() instead of the raw switch, because that message goes to the page's console and would otherwise announce software WebGL on every GPU-less launch. verdict_reason: TextMetrics is a measurement, not a stored value. Every field is a pure function of (the font binary that was matched, the shaper, the font-size/letter-spacing/direction state), and text_metrics.cc:95-170 performs no arithmetic that is not one of those. It is therefore correct exactly when its INPUTS are correct — fonts.installed, fonts.generic-families and the subpixel-positioning flag — and there is nothing to replay, because the value depends on the string the detector chose. A1 forbids intercepting the accessor and A3 forbids perturbing the result, and here the second prohibition has teeth: the T0 values are exact binary fractions (width 103.599609375 = 212172/2048) because macOS shaping is unhinted and linear, so a rounded or noised metric is not merely wrong, it is a positive identification of tampering. notes: Escalated, and for a real reason rather than for ownership. What is unresolved: the fallback font is chosen by the host text engine (CoreText on macOS, fontconfig behind the browser-process font service on Linux) out of the fonts that are actually on disk. It cannot be made to equal a macOS reference device from a Linux host by any patch, because there is no Apple Color Emoji, no Times and no Lucida Grande to fall back TO, and the advance widths the detector measures come out of the font binary. Two candidate resolutions, and they have very different costs: (a) restrict profiles to hosts whose OS matches the claim, which makes this row 'inherit' and makes coh.platform-resource-sets cheap; (b) ship a redistributable font bundle per claimed platform and pin fallback to it, which is a licensing question before it is an engineering one and still will not reproduce Apple's metrics. What would settle it: capture probes['fonts.detected'] and probes['canvas.2d'].measureText on a Linux host running stock Chrome, and diff the miss widths and the emoji-bearing measureText width against the macOS capture we already hold. If they differ — and they will — option (a) is the only honest answer and the project scope changes. That measurement costs one collector run. MEASURED: the escalate asked whether a Linux host can serve a macOS font profile at all. It can. Given the same font file both platforms produce the same metrics; the divergence is font availability and glyph selection, not the rasteriser or the VDMX path. So the requirement is 'install the claimed platform's fonts', which is ordinary work, not 'host OS must match claimed OS'. Patch 0095 serves the Windows script fallback table (74 entries) under a Windows profile. evidence.note: Menlo's advance is 1233/2048 em; 12 chars * 24px * 1233/2048 = 355104/2048 = 173.390625 EXACTLY. The measured client rect is the unrounded sum of twelve font-unit advances, which simultaneously proves that monospace resolves to Menlo, that macOS shaping is linear and unhinted, and that any noise added here would be arithmetically detectable.

SkFontGetGlyphWidthForHarfBuzz: sk_width = strike_ref.getWidth(glyph), and then `if (!subpixel) sk_width = SkScalarRoundToInt(sk_width)`. One boolean decides whether every advance in the browser is an exact fraction or an integer.
HarfBuzzGetGlyphHorizontalAdvance passes hb_font_data->font_.isSubpixel() as that boolean, so the SkFont's subpixel flag is the switch

CreateSkFont sets should_subpixel_position = true unconditionally on macOS (only WebTestSupport can clear it), then setSubpixel and setLinearMetrics from it, with a comment noting CoreText always supplies linear metrics anyway. macOS advances are therefore always fractional.

on Linux and Windows the equivalent flags come from RendererPreferences, i.e. from the host's fontconfig and desktop settings in the BROWSER process. So on those platforms a host setting silently quantises every advance width in the page.

notes: This row exists to name the single boolean that decides whether text geometry is fractional or integral everywhere at once. On macOS it is a hard-coded true and nothing can move it. On Linux it is host state: a machine with subpixel positioning off produces integer advances throughout, which contradicts a macOS claim in every getClientRects and every measureText call simultaneously and cannot be repaired in either surface. That makes it a profile-loader concern — set the RendererPreferences font fields from the profile rather than from the host — even though the row itself is 'inherit'. Feeds layout.client-rects (screen-geometry) and canvas.measure-text directly, which is why both are listed as coherence members rather than as notes. Served at 0122: that boolean is fonts.render_params.subpixel_positioning, and gfx::GetFontRenderParams returns the profile's whole tuple in every process, so on Linux it is no longer the host's fontconfig answer postprocessed by this display's scale factor, and on macOS it is no longer the hard-coded constant. What 0122 must NOT do is move an advance, which is why the advance is measured rather than assumed: on the pre-patch macos-arm64 build the two personas agreed at 16px Helvetica 177.9296875, 28px Georgia 252.08203125 and 13.5px Arial 134.347412109375, and those are the numbers the served build has to reproduce. Integer ascent and descent and glyph ink boxes do differ per persona, which is patch 0040's Apple font metric policy serving coh.font-metrics-platform-rounding and not this row.

verdict_reason: An advance sum is computed, not stored. HarfBuzz asks Skia for each glyph's width and Skia reads it out of the font binary; there is no intermediate value that could be replaced without lying about the font. It becomes correct when fonts.installed and fonts.generic-families are correct, and perturbing it is the same self-inflicted tell as perturbing client rects — worse here, because the T0 values are exact rational multiples of the font's unitsPerEm and any offset shows up as a non-representable fraction. Listed so the path is recognisably off-limits.

notes: This row corrects a widely held assumption. Every anti-detect writeup that treats navigator.storage.estimate().quota as 'about 60% of free disk' is describing pre-M110 Chrome; at 152 the free-space term is gone entirely and even total space only matters below 10 GiB. The practical consequences are the reverse of the usual advice: (1) there is nothing to spoof here and a tool that writes a plausible disk-derived number into quota produces a value stock Chrome cannot emit; (2) the only way to get a wrong answer is to run in incognito or on a tiny volume; (3) quota is usage-additive, so a site that has written 100 MB legitimately sees 10 GiB + 100 MB and a fixed 10 GiB response to every caller is itself the anomaly. The V3 check is an equality against 10737418240 + usage rather than a range.
observable: (await navigator.storage.estimate()).quota

The host value is therefore already exactly the reference value - a constant 10737418240 for a fresh origin - and carries no host information to spoof. The residual risk is a container or VM with a volume smaller than 10 GiB, where the answer becomes ceil(total/1GiB)*1GiB and does leak the host; that is a deployment constraint recorded as coh.reported-quota-is-static-not-disk, not a value to patch.

notes: Escalated because the honest answer depends on a decision this shard cannot make. The values themselves are device state and inheriting them is right on a host with a real battery, which is what the M4 Max capture shows. The problem is the other host: a datacentre VM has no battery, so getBattery() resolves the mojom defaults exactly - {charging: true, level: 1, chargingTime: 0, dischargingTime: Infinity} - and that tuple contradicts a profile claiming a MacBook. What makes this an escalation rather than a patch is that the same tuple is perfectly correct for a real iMac, Mac Studio, Mac mini or desktop PC, so the cheap fix is a profile constraint - desktop profiles on battery-less hosts, laptop profiles only on hosts with batteries - and no code at all. What would settle it: a ruling on whether laptop profiles must be servable from battery-less hosts. If they must, this becomes a hard problem rather than a value to set, because axiom A3 forbids per-call randomness while a battery that reads 0.24 for an hour and then 0.24 again tomorrow is itself the tell; a synthesised battery needs a monotonic, wall-clock-driven discharge model with the chargingTime/dischargingTime multiple-of-60 invariant preserved, and that is a design task deserving its own row. Note also the derived constraints a detector can check for free: exactly one of chargingTime and dischargingTime is finite, and the finite one is always a multiple of 60. RULING (this session, patch 0089): presence is keyed on the claimed chassis — desktops emit the real no-battery tuple, laptops emit a plausible level and discharging time, and nothing animates within a launch. THE CPU DEPENDENCE. FftPlanner::new() selects, at runtime, FftPlannerAvx -> FftPlannerSse -> FftPlannerNeon -> FftPlannerWasmSimd -> FftPlannerScalar. avx_planner.rs:124-126 requires is_x86_feature_detected!("avx") && is_x86_feature_detected!("fma"). third_party/rust/rustfft/v6/BUILD.gn:91-95 enables the avx, sse and neon features, so all four kernels are compiled in and the choice is made by the host CPU.

the kernels are not arithmetically equivalent. AVX uses fmadd/fmaddsub (one rounding), NEON uses vfmaq_f32 (one rounding), SSE uses _mm_add_ps(acc, _mm_mul_ps(a, b)) (two roundings). Same input, different float32 output. -ffp-contract=off does not touch explicit FMA intrinsics.

a second, independent architecture split: OscillatorHandler::ProcessKRateVector and ProcessARateVectorKernel have three separate bodies - SSE2 on x86/x64, NEON on arm/arm64, and a scalar fallback at oscillator_handler.cc:357 and :368 for everything else. The SSE2 file documents the divergence in its own comment at :115-117 ("Ideally, to preserve accuracy, we should use (two) packed double vectors for this, but that degrades performance quite a bit") and again at :188 ("There's a bit of round-off above").

THE OS DEPENDENCE. Both calls are UNQUALIFIED - sin(static_cast<double>(kPiOverTwoFloat * compressor_gain)) in the per-sample gain warp, and exp(...) in KneeCurve - so they bind to the host libm from <cmath>, not to fdlibm. The same file uses fdlibm::powf at :145 and fdlibm::asinf at :190, so this is an inconsistency in Chromium rather than a deliberate choice.

DecibelsToLinear returns powf(10, 0.05f*decibels) and LinearToDecibels returns 20*log10f(linear) - both unqualified host-libm float functions, in a file that includes fdlibm/ieee754.h and uses fdlibm::exp at :69. These are on the compressor's per-sample metering path (dynamics_compressor.cc:337) and inside Saturate/KneeCurve, so a 1-ULP libm difference feeds metering_gain_ -> db_compression_diff -> envelope_rate -> compressor_gain -> the output samples.

-ffp-contract=off is applied unconditionally under is_clang, so the COMPILER never fuses a*b+c on its own. This rules out compiler-introduced FMA divergence and leaves exactly two mechanisms: explicit FMA intrinsics inside rustfft/NEON, and the host libm.

vector_math picks its backend at COMPILE time - mac (Accelerate vDSP) / neon / x86 / scalar. Vsmul and Vmaxmgv, the two operations CreateBandLimitedTables uses, are exactly-rounded per element in every backend, so this split does not by itself change the render. cpu/x86/vector_math_x86.h:29-30 adds a RUNTIME base::CPU().has_avx() dispatch which does matter for the order-dependent reductions used elsewhere in the graph.

the pre-RustFFT backends are still compiled in and still OS-split - Accelerate vDSP on Mac (vDSP_fft_zrip at fft_frame_mac.cc:138,154), PFFFT everywhere else, guarded by #if !BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC). Disabling WebAudioRustFft therefore changes the render wholesale and deterministically. It is a Chromium-version lever, not a device lever.

notes: THE ESCALATION for WebRTC. These two rows are codec facts, not network facts, so they belong here rather than in subsystem 9 - but the values are produced in the GPU process from real hardware encoder and decoder enumeration, so patching them belongs wherever GPUInfo and the media capabilities are already being set for gpu.angle-backend. That is the recommendation: do not patch the Blink serialisers (A1 forbids it and there are four of them), set the claimed device's encode/decode profile set at the GPU-process source and let both getCapabilities calls, decodingInfo's powerEfficient, and the SDP a real connection would offer all follow from one place. WHAT IS UNRESOLVED: we hold one T0 capture, so we cannot tell which parts of these lists are hardware and which are libwebrtc constants. The cheap experiment that separates them: capture the same probe on the same machine with --disable-accelerated-video-encode and --disable-accelerated-video-decode. Everything that survives is software and constant; everything that moves is the hardware term, and that term is exactly what a profile has to carry. Note also that the sender/receiver asymmetry is itself the check - a fork that spoofs one list and not the other produces a machine whose encoder is broader than its decoder, which no real device is.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH. P2PSocketManager::DoGetNetworkList is net::GetNetworkList(&list, net::EXCLUDE_HOST_SCOPE_VIRTUAL_INTERFACES) running in the NETWORK SERVICE. It is a raw getifaddrs(3) of the host, with no reference to the proxy configuration, the URLRequestContext's proxy resolution service, or anything else the --proxy-server switch touches. A configured proxy constrains this list by exactly nothing.
The macOS/POSIX GetNetworkList. Each interface yields name, friendly_name, interface_index, ConnectionType, IPAddress, prefix_length, ip_address_attributes and an optional EUI-48 MAC address.

MULTI-PROCESS AND PROXY-BLIND. GetDefaultLocalAddress learns the default route by creating a DatagramClientSocket from url_request_context_->GetNetworkSessionContext()->client_socket_factory and ConnectAsync-ing it to the hardcoded constants 8.8.8.8:53 / 2001:4860:4860::8888:53, then reading GetLocalAddress(). This is the plain socket factory, not proxy_resolving_socket_factory_, so the 'default local address' that later becomes a host candidate is a readout of the HOST's routing table.

FIFTH CONFIRMED MULTI-PROCESS DUPLICATION. The whole net::NetworkInterfaceList - interface names such as en0/utun4, MAC addresses, prefix lengths, connection types - is serialised over mojo from the network service into the RENDERER, where IpcNetworkManager converts it to webrtc::Network objects. The renderer holds a full copy of the host's network topology before any filtering is applied.
CreatePortAllocator is where the four IP handling policy modes become P2PPortAllocator::Config, and where the choice between FilteringNetworkManager and EmptyNetworkManager is made.
corpus_coverage is absent because the collector cannot see this surface at all. See notes for the exact probe needed.

evidence.note: MEASURED, and the defect this patch exists for. Through a residential SOCKS5 exit whose host has an A record and no AAAA record, the IPv6 wildcard UDP port was created, its socket was refused with -109 ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE at the resolution stage, and the port then appeared exactly twice in a --v=1 log -- 'Port created' and 'Added port to allocator' -- with no 'Port ready.', no 'Gathered candidate' and no 'Port completed gathering candidates.'. iceGatheringState was still 'gathering' after 50 s and the null end-of-candidates candidate never fired. The IPv4 pair (1 mDNS host + 1 srflx 46.175.127.114) was correct and complete throughout, so the candidate COUNT was right for a v4-only egress and the missing completion signal was the whole defect.
evidence.source: own measurement, Apostate v0.1.0 through proxy.geonode.io:12000, CDP gatherer /tmp/nr/drive.js, logs /tmp/nr/apostate-proxy*.stderr.log

evidence.note: THE DESIGN. A relayed socket has no family of its own: the only address it ever sends to is its association's relay endpoint, and the ICE candidate it produces is that endpoint verbatim, so its local bind family, its transport family and its candidate family are all the relay's. Hence the families offered to WebRTC are the families the configured proxy resolves in -- {IPv4} for proxy.geonode.io, measured; both for a proxy with an AAAA record -- and the decision is taken in the network service before any port exists, not by killing a port's socket afterwards. The destination of a relayed datagram lives in the RFC 1928 per-datagram header and is independent of the local socket family, so no second local family is ever needed.

REFERENCE SHAPE, measured. Stock Chrome 153 on a dual-stack macOS host with no proxy and media permission denied: 4 candidates, 2 mDNS .local host candidates (priority 2113937151 IPv4, 2113939711 IPv6) and 2 srflx literals, one per family, each on its family's host port, gathering complete in about 1 s. Apostate v0.1.0 with a Windows persona and no proxy matched field for field, so the direct path was already clean and is unchanged by this patch.

notes: THE KEY A PATCH WOULD NEED IS network.local_interfaces, which is undeclared. THE CENTRAL ROW OF THIS SHARD, and it is a leak row rather than a fingerprint row. Under axiom A1 the patch belongs at emit.network.p2p-socket-manager-do-get-network-list plus emit.network.p2p-socket-manager-get-default-local-address, in the network service: replace the enumerated interface list and the default local address with the profile's claimed ones. Doing it there rather than in Blink means the FilteringNetworkManager/EmptyNetworkManager split, the mDNS obfuscation, the priority computation and the SDP serialisation all follow by construction, and it means the renderer never receives the host's real interface names or MAC addresses in the first place. Patching in the renderer would leave the network service still holding and still binding to the real interfaces. NOTE the ordering constraint: the profile's interface list has to be ordered the way webrtc::NetworkManagerBase::MergeNetworkList would order the real one, because the sort position becomes the candidate priority (see webrtc.candidate-network-metadata). COLLECTOR REQUEST, precise: a probe 'webrtc.ice' that constructs `new RTCPeerConnection({iceServers:[{urls:'stun:stun.l.google.com:19302'}]})`, calls createDataChannel('probe') and createOffer/setLocalDescription, collects every candidate until iceGatheringState becomes 'complete' or a 5s timeout, and records for each: the raw candidate string, type, protocol, address, port, priority, foundation, relatedAddress, relatedPort, and the parsed network-id / network-cost extensions; plus the final iceGatheringState and the elapsed time to complete. Without it this row and five others in this shard cannot reach V3. It should also be run a second time with no iceServers, to separate host gathering from STUN gathering. Patch 0086 changes only the egress, not the interface list: P2PSocketManager::DoGetNetworkList still returns the host's real interfaces, which is the remaining half of this row and a separate patch. No status change. Patch 0086 reached V1 (all eleven files accounted for), but patch_id stays NULL on this row deliberately: 0086 changes the EGRESS, not the interface list, and P2PSocketManager::DoGetNetworkList still returns the host's real interfaces. That is the remaining half of this row and a separate patch. The row carries 0086's relay-address emitter because the relayed candidate's address does come from it, which is the join the emitter index is for — patch_id is for the patch that implements the row, and 0086 implements half of it. PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by 0118, which does not touch the interface list itself and so leaves the paragraph above standing: the network service still enumerates the host's real interfaces and the renderer still receives them. What 0118 changes is which ADDRESS FAMILIES are offered. A family whose datagrams have no egress is dropped from the merged interface list in IpcNetworkManager and refused in IpcPacketSocketFactory, so no port of that family is ever created. Replacing the list is still the open work and still a separate patch.

evidence.note: BASE_FEATURE(kWebRtcHideLocalIpsWithMdns, base::FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT) - so mDNS obfuscation is the stock default, gated additionally on BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_MDNS) at peer_connection_dependency_factory.cc:790

SOURCE OF TRUTH for the name. RandomUuidNameGenerator::CreateName returns base::Uuid::GenerateRandomV4().AsLowercaseString(), and CreateNameForAddress appends '.local'. The name is cached per address in name_addr_map_ for the life of that MdnsResponder, and creating one sends real multicast announcements on the LAN (kMinNumAnnouncementsToSend, one second apart).

THE CONDITIONAL THAT MATTERS. GetMdnsResponder returns nullptr when enumeration_permission() == ENUMERATION_ALLOWED or when allow_mdns_obfuscation_ is false. Enumeration becomes ALLOWED as soon as EITHER microphone or camera permission is granted (CheckPermission at :132-149 fires both HasPermission checks and :160 sets ALLOWED on the first grant). So a page that holds getUserMedia permission sees the real local IPv4/IPv6 addresses, not .local names.

MaybeObfuscateAddress applies only when c.is_local(), i.e. host candidates. SanitizeCandidate then replaces the address with the hostname and empties related_address. Server-reflexive and relay candidates are NOT obfuscated - see webrtc.srflx-candidate.
allow_mdns_obfuscation is set false only for origins matching prefs::kWebRtcLocalIpsAllowedUrls, an enterprise-policy list that is empty by default.

notes: Resolved as inherit, but with two obligations recorded as edges rather than as changes here. (1) mDNS hides the ADDRESS and nothing else: the number of host candidates still equals the number of enumerated interfaces, and each still carries a priority, a network-id and a network-cost that describe that interface. See webrtc.candidate-network-metadata. (2) The obfuscation switches itself off the moment a capture permission is granted, at which point webrtc.ice-candidates must already be correct or the profile is contradicted in one step. Do not treat mDNS as the mitigation for the leak; it is a stock behaviour we must merely not break.
observable: For each host-type ICE candidate, whether RTCIceCandidate.address is a dotted-quad / IPv6 literal or a '<uuid>.local' hostname, and the shape of that hostname
verdict_reason: Stock Chrome 152 already obfuscates host candidates by default: blink::features::kWebRtcHideLocalIpsWithMdns is FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT, and the name is a fresh random UUIDv4 generated in the network service with no device-derived entropy. The emitted value is therefore already independent of the host, which is the definition of inherit. Disabling it or replacing it with a synthesised name would both be departures from the reference device.

evidence.note: THE FORK. P2PSocket::Create takes a ProxyResolvingClientSocketFactory* and hands it to P2PSocketTcp and P2PSocketStunTcp - and NOT to P2PSocketUdp, whose constructor does not receive it. P2P_SOCKET_UDP is the only branch that gets no proxy factory.

SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE LEAK. P2PSocketUdp::Init calls socket_->Listen(local_address) on a plain net::UDPSocket and then sends STUN binding requests straight out of it. Grepping the whole file for 'proxy' returns nothing. There is no proxy consultation on this path at any point.

UDPPort::OnStunBindingRequestSucceeded turns the STUN server's MAPPED-ADDRESS into an srflx candidate via AddAddress(..., IceCandidateType::kSrflx, ...). Port::MaybeObfuscateAddress at port.cc:259 returns false for anything that is not is_local(), so this address is emitted verbatim - there is no mDNS equivalent for srflx.

The comment on the DISABLE_ADAPTER_ENUMERATION path reads: 'we'll just bind to any address instead of specific NIC. This is to ensure the same routing for http traffic BY OS is also used here to avoid any local or public IP leakage during stun process.' The word is OS, not proxy. Binding to the ANY address routes through the host's default route, which under an HTTP or SOCKS proxy is still the host's real ISP path.

Therefore, in every IP handling mode except disable_non_proxied_udp - including the stock default - a page that supplies any STUN server learns the machine's real public IP regardless of --proxy-server. This is a deanonymisation, not a fingerprint mismatch.

notes: ESCALATED, and it is the most serious finding in this shard. WHAT IS UNRESOLVED is not whether the leak exists - the source settles that - but which of exactly three remedies the project takes, because each has a different cost and each is owned jointly with subsystem 10. (a) Route P2P UDP through the proxy. This is precisely the SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE work already designed for QUIC in docs/subsystems/network-proxy.md; the substitution point here is the DatagramClientSocket created in P2PSocketUdp::Init rather than QuicSessionPool::CreateSocket, and the same association-lifetime and peer-address hazards apply. This is the only remedy that keeps the candidate set shaped like stock Chrome. (b) Force disable_non_proxied_udp. Cheap, no leak, but it deletes every UDP host and srflx candidate and every TURN/UDP relay candidate, leaving only TCP candidates - a candidate set no ordinary Chrome installation produces. That is the same class of tell as the missing QUIC attempt in subsystem 10: perfect at the JavaScript layer, wrong one layer down. (c) Substitute the claimed public address at emit.webrtc.udp-port-stun-binding-succeeded. This violates A1 twice over - it fakes an observation rather than the code path that makes it, and it does not stop the packet, so the STUN server still sees the real address and any detector who runs their own STUN server sees the truth while the JavaScript sees the lie, which is strictly worse than the leak. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a V4 run under a SOCKS5 proxy with the collector's proposed webrtc.ice probe pointed at a STUN server we control, comparing the srflx address in the candidate against the source address the server actually saw. Recommendation is (a), with (b) as the interim posture while (a) is built - and (b) must then be declared in the ledger as a known class-level tell rather than as a fix. DECIDED by patch 0086: proxy the UDP when the configured proxy can relay a datagram, fail closed when it cannot, and never accept the public-IP leak. The row stays OPEN because 0086 is compile-unverified and no live-proxy run has been made, so there is no T0 evidence for the after-state; achieved_tier is V0 because the patch applies in series order and has not been built. V1: all eleven files of patch 0086 are accounted for — five translation units (socks5_datagram_server_socket.cc, datagram_server_socket.cc, socket_udp.cc, socket.cc, socket_manager.cc) plus the one-line switch-array entry in chrome_content_browser_client.cc, three headers that are not translation units, and net/BUILD.gn. All four signature risks flagged for this patch (GrowableIOBuffer::span_before_offset, IOBuffer::span, the IPAddress(base::span) constructor and HostResolver::CreateRequest) are in socks5_datagram_server_socket.cc, which compiled. PROVENANCE CAVEAT, recorded rather than hidden: chrome_content_browser_client.cc reported OK in 39 seconds because an earlier gate invocation had already built that object against this same tree state before the shell holding it died. It is a genuine compile of the current content, not an inherited pass from an older tree, but it is not a fresh compile in the reporting invocation. DECISION (mine, asked for by the gate owner): do not spend the ~40 minutes deleting the object and recompiling. The distinction that matters — whether the bytes compiled were today's — is settled; re-running would relabel a verified compile rather than test anything, and the tier this establishes is V1, which is a compile and nothing more. If a reader wants it unambiguous the object is deletable and the re-run is cheap in money if not in minutes. Compile only: no build, no run, and no live-proxy observation, which is what keeps this row open. THE WAVE'S ONE REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND HERE, and it is worth the row carrying it: an unused kWebRtcUdpBlockValue constant turned out to be masking a silent fallback in which any unrecognised --fingerprint-webrtc-udp value was rounded to `block`. A typo'd switch value therefore produced the fail-closed posture silently instead of refusing the launch, which is the same silent-fallback shape patch 0081's refusals were introduced to remove. 38 translation units compiled across the wave to surface exactly this one defect, which is the argument for the compile gate rather than against it. 0086 took remedy (a) and closed the leak. 0118 fixes what remedy (a) left behind: the family a relayed srflx candidate can be in is the proxy's, not the host's, so only families the proxy resolves in are offered and the candidate set is the shape an IPv4-only desktop emits instead of a truncated dual-stack one that never finishes gathering.

evidence.note: IpcPacketSocketFactory::CreateClientTcpSocket maps the webrtc transport request onto P2P_SOCKET_TCP_CLIENT / SSLTCP / TLS_CLIENT and their STUN_ variants. turn: with transport=tcp and turns: land here; turn: with transport=udp goes to CreateUdpSocket at :805.

SOURCE OF TRUTH for whether the proxy is honoured. The comment 'GetPeerAddress returns ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED if the socket is connected through a proxy' and the tolerance of that error at :181 confirm the proxied case is a supported, exercised path here.

evidence.note: The four modes and their exact pref strings: 'default', 'default_public_and_private_interfaces', 'default_public_interface_only', 'disable_non_proxied_udp'. ToWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy falls through to kDefault for any unrecognised string.

THE STOCK DEFAULT, verified: RegisterStringPref(prefs::kWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy, blink::kWebRTCIPHandlingDefault) - i.e. 'default'. Nothing narrows it unless enterprise policy (configuration_policy_handler_list_factory.cc:935), the extensions privacy API (pref_mapping.cc:90), a per-URL entry in kWebRTCIPHandlingUrl, or the --webrtc-ip-handling-policy switch (chrome_command_line_pref_store.cc:55) sets it.

WHAT EACH MODE ACTUALLY DOES, at the source. kDefault: enable_multiple_routes=true, enable_nonproxied_udp=true -> FilteringNetworkManager. kDefaultPublicAndPrivateInterfaces: multiple_routes=false, nonproxied_udp=true, enable_default_local_candidate=TRUE -> EmptyNetworkManager. kDefaultPublicInterfaceOnly: identical except enable_default_local_candidate=FALSE. kDisableNonProxiedUdp: multiple_routes=false, nonproxied_udp=FALSE -> EmptyNetworkManager. Note the two middle modes differ by exactly one boolean.

AND HOW THOSE BOOLEANS BECOME BEHAVIOUR. !enable_multiple_routes -> PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_ADAPTER_ENUMERATION. !enable_default_local_candidate -> PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_DEFAULT_LOCAL_CANDIDATE. !enable_nonproxied_udp -> PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_UDP | PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_STUN | PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_UDP_RELAY, all three at once. set_allow_tcp_listen(false) is unconditional.

With adapter enumeration disabled the session uses GetAnyAddressNetworks() - a single 0.0.0.0 and a single :: network - and UDPPort::MaybeSetDefaultLocalAddress substitutes the default local address into the host candidate when emit_local_for_anyaddress is set. That is how default_public_and_private_interfaces still exposes one private address while default_public_interface_only exposes none.

The Config comment on enable_nonproxied_udp: 'When set to false, it effectively disables all UDP traffic until UDP-supporting proxy RETURN is available in the future.' Chromium itself documents that the safe mode is a capability gap, not a design.

notes: ESCALATED because the choice of mode is a policy decision for the arbiter and it is not free in any direction. The stock reference device produces host/udp (mDNS-named), srflx/udp when a STUN server is offered, and relay candidates over whichever transports the TURN server offers. Selecting disable_non_proxied_udp removes the first two entirely and is trivially detectable by a script that offers a public STUN server and observes that no srflx candidate ever arrives while the connection still reaches 'complete'. Selecting default_public_interface_only removes host candidates but leaves the srflx leak untouched, so it costs coherence and buys nothing - it is the mode most anti-detect tools reach for and it is the wrong one. The honest options are the two named in webrtc.srflx-candidate. Recording the source-level table above is the durable output of this row: the four modes are not four privacy levels, they are three settings of two independent booleans plus one that turns UDP off wholesale. patch_id and V1 recorded for 0086: ResolveUdpEgress decides whether a UDP candidate of this type exists at all, and 0086's emitters name this row as a surface they produce. Either way gathering completes with no UDP candidate and TURN over TCP or TLS still works. The observation in the notes above -- that no srflx ever arriving while the connection still reaches 'complete' is detectable -- is unchanged and is the cost of a proxy that cannot relay datagrams.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE WIRE FORM. Candidate::ToString appends ' network-id <id>' whenever network_id() > 0 and ' network-cost <cost>' whenever network_cost() > 0, directly into the a=candidate line that JavaScript reads from RTCIceCandidate.candidate. Neither is redacted by anything.

THE HOLE IN mDNS. Candidate::ToSanitizedCopy rewrites only address, related_address and optionally username. priority, foundation, network_id and network_cost survive obfuscation untouched, so a candidate whose address is a random .local hostname still states which interface it came from and how that interface ranks.
MergeNetworkList sorts the interfaces and then assigns preference 127, 126, 125 ... in order. So the local-preference byte of every candidate's priority is (127 - rank of its interface).

priority = (type_pref << 24) | (((network_adapter_preference << 8) | IPAddressPrecedence(addr)) + relay_pref) << 8 | (256 - component). The interface rank is therefore recoverable from the priority of any candidate by arithmetic, and the count of distinct ranks is the number of interfaces.

network-cost is a direct readout of the ADAPTER TYPE: 0 ethernet/loopback, 10 wifi, 50 unknown, 250/500/910/980 for 5G/4G/3G/2G cellular, 999 for a type the manager deliberately refuses to name, +1 if the interface is a VPN. A single integer in the SDP says whether the machine is on ethernet, wifi, cellular or VPN.

The adapter type is derived in the renderer from net::NetworkInterface::type, falling back to webrtc::GetAdapterTypeFromName(it->name) - string matching on the real interface name - and is forced to ADAPTER_TYPE_VPN when IsVpnMacAddress(*it->mac_address) matches, i.e. from the host MAC's OUI.
net->set_id(next_available_network_id_++) - network-id is a small sequential integer, so the highest network-id seen is a lower bound on how many interfaces the host has ever had during the session.

notes: THE KEY A PATCH WOULD NEED IS network.local_interfaces, which is undeclared - the same single patch as webrtc.ice-candidates, in the network service. NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT, and it is the reason mDNS is not a solution. A detector that never learns a single IP address can still read, from an offer SDP alone: how many network interfaces the machine has, how they rank against each other, whether each is ethernet / wifi / cellular / VPN, and - by the VPN bit at ipc_network_manager.cc:130 - whether a VPN adapter with a recognised MAC prefix is present. A machine that reports one wifi interface, or three interfaces of which one is flagged VPN, has described itself precisely. The fix is the same single patch as webrtc.ice-candidates and that is the argument for placing it in the network service: replacing the interface list there sets the count, the order, the types and hence every one of these fields consistently. Replacing them anywhere downstream means reproducing MergeNetworkList's sort by hand and getting the same answer, which is strictly harder and easy to get subtly wrong. Coherence obligation with subsystem 3: if the profile claims a laptop the interface set should look like a laptop's, and network-cost 0 on every interface (all-ethernet) on a machine whose profile claims a MacBook is an internal contradiction.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH. When min_port == 0 - the default, since prefs::kWebRTCUDPPortRange registers as an empty string at browser_ui_prefs.cc:158 and ParsePortRange leaves both at 0 - Init calls socket_->Listen(local_address) with port 0 and the OS picks. The candidate port is therefore drawn from the HOST kernel's ephemeral port range, in the network service.

THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS LEVER. When a range IS configured, the loop is `for (port = min_port; port <= max_port && result < 0; ++port)` - it binds the LOWEST FREE PORT, ascending, deterministically. Setting --webrtc-udp-port-range to a plausible macOS range would therefore produce candidates on 49152, 49153, 49154 ... which is a far louder signal than an out-of-range port, because no kernel allocates ephemeral ports that way.

Marked T3 deliberately - these are widely known defaults but we have measured none of them ourselves, and net_preferred_port_range is host-configurable. The magnitude of the signal is unknown until measured.

notes: Kept as its own row rather than folded into webrtc.ice-candidates because it is the cheapest V3 regression check in this shard: if a patch to the network manager accidentally produces an empty or never-terminating gathering sequence, this row fails first and unambiguously. THIS ROW FAILED FIRST AND UNAMBIGUOUSLY, exactly as written above, and it was patch 0086 that broke it. 0118 fixes it three ways: the families with no egress are never offered, so the doomed port is not created; a socket the renderer knows will be refused is refused synchronously, which webrtc handles on every port type; and UDPPort now subscribes to its socket's close event, so a socket that dies for any other reason -- a proxy that answers ASSOCIATE with REP 0x07, a control connection that drops mid-handshake -- errors its port instead of pending for ever. The salt is persistent per storage key via MediaDeviceSaltService if and only if cookie_settings->IsFullCookieAccessAllowed for this frame; otherwise the ephemeral BrowserContext::UniqueId() is used and are_persistent_device_ids_allowed is false.

When persistence is not allowed the per-document frame_salt is appended, and that frame salt is regenerated on every navigation (media_device_id_salt_base_ = CreateRandomMediaDeviceIDSalt()). notes: Resolved as inherit, and it EXTENDS media.device-counts rather than restating it. Three things fall out that the audio shard could not see from the counts alone. (1) The pre-permission shape is a constant: one entry per kind with three empty strings. Any profile whose spoofed device list is applied at the audio-service end automatically reproduces it, and any implementation that instead fabricates deviceIds in the renderer will emit non-empty ids without permission, which is a decisive tell. (2) Once permission IS granted the full list appears with real HMACs, so the count that matters for V3 is the post-permission one and the corpus currently holds only the pre-permission one - the collector should gain a permission-granted variant of the media.devices probe, run under --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream, to capture it. (3) Because the transform is deterministic in the raw id, the raw ids the patched device list supplies must be STABLE for the life of the profile: a raw id regenerated per call would make deviceId change between two enumerateDevices() calls in one document, which axiom A3 forbids and no real device does.
observable: MediaDeviceInfo.deviceId for each entry of navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices() - its format, its stability across repeated calls, across reloads and across sessions, and its value before any capture permission is granted
verdict_reason: The emitted value is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the requesting origin over (raw device id || per-storage-key salt), hex-encoded lowercase. It is a 64-character string with no host-derived structure, it differs per origin, and it is uncorrelated with the underlying hardware. There is nothing in the value to make correct that is not already correct. What must be true is a property of the raw device list rather than of this transform, and that belongs to media.device-counts.

evidence.note: SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE ASYMMETRY. group_id_salt = StrCat({salt, frame_salt, "group_id"}) - the per-document frame_salt is mixed in UNCONDITIONALLY, whereas device_id_salt appends it only when persistent ids are disallowed. The comment states the intent: 'must be unique per document, but it must also change if cookies are cleared'.
An empty raw group_id is passed through as an empty string rather than hashed, so a device whose backend supplies no group id is distinguishable from one that does.

Video group ids are back-filled from a heuristic that matches camera names against audio device group ids - which is why MediaDevicesDispatcherHost::OnVideoGotSaltAndOrigin at :399-402 requests audio devices even when only video was asked for. The camera-microphone grouping on a laptop is manufactured by that heuristic, not read from hardware.

notes: Left open rather than resolved because it states a requirement on the spoofed device list that nothing else in the ledger states, and we cannot check it without a permission-granted capture. On a real laptop the built-in camera and the built-in microphone share a groupId, produced by the name-matching heuristic above; a spoofed device list that gives them independent raw group ids produces a machine whose webcam and mic are separate USB peripherals, which contradicts a claimed MacBook. Conversely a spoofed list whose group ids are all identical claims every device is one physical unit. The correct behaviour is to carry raw group ids in the profile alongside the raw device ids and let the existing HMAC do the rest. Also worth recording as a live detection: because groupId is salted per document and deviceId is not (when cookies are allowed), a page can compare the two across a reload and learn its own cookie-permission state - stock behaviour, but a fork that made deviceId per-document to look 'safer' would break the asymmetry and be detectable by exactly that comparison.

verdict_reason: groupId is the same HMAC transform as deviceId over the raw group id, differing only in which salt is mixed in, so the emitted string carries no host-derived structure either. What it encodes is a relation - which devices are physically the same unit - and that relation is a property of the raw device list produced by the audio and video capture services, not of this code. It is correct once the device list is correct.

evidence.note: THE CORRECTION. On real headed Chrome 152 with no extension matching the page, window.chrome has exactly three keys and chrome.runtime is ABSENT. resources/surfaces.json rates chrome.runtime 'high' and says 'absence is a headless tell'; that is exactly backwards for a plain web page in 2026. in a webpage context, runtime is added only if CanWebpageContextConnectExternally(context) - i.e. some installed extension names this URL in externally_connectable - or if some other web-available feature was exposed. chrome.app is explicitly excluded from that second test ('chrome.app is exposed to all webpages, we ignore it for this check'), which is why app is present and runtime is not.

LoadTimesBindings::Install runs from DidCreateScriptContext for every world, and uses content::GetOrCreateChromeObject, so window.chrome exists in isolated worlds too and is created lazily by whichever installer runs first
the same bindings are installed on service worker contexts when AllowScriptExtensionForServiceWorker, so chrome.loadTimes exists in a service worker as well - a scope a shim would forget

evidence.note: BEFORE STATE. Attaching a session alone changes nothing a page can read. evidence.note: THE ONE REAL LEAK. upstream reads the own descriptor first and declines when its get is not a builtin getter, which is what already defeats the canonical probe. every getErrorProperty call there is already guarded by ToLocal with a fallback, and for name the fallback is v8::Object::GetConstructorName, the value that function prefers anyway. evidence.note: ANSWERS THIS ROW'S OPEN QUESTION. The limit does track installed memory, but the mapping saturates. jsHeapSizeLimit read 4395630592 bytes precisely, which is what a site-locked page gets, and 3760000000 after Blink's bucketing elsewhere, identically for every profile in the current 8-32 GiB pool and identically in all three attach states. So it is neither attach-dependent nor a per-platform constant: it is installed memory halved and clamped to 4 GiB, which means it only diverges from the claim when the host or the claim falls below 8 GiB.
evidence.source: measured on the shipped apostate-152.0.7977.83-macos-arm64 artifact, 36 GiB host

evidence.note: old generation is physical memory over 2 clamped to Heap::kDefaultMaxHeapSize of 4 GiB, and HeapStatistics::heap_size_limit is Heap::MaxReserved over that. base::SysInfo::AmountOfTotalPhysicalMemory is not spoofed anywhere in the series, so before patch 0087 this was the host's figure. A 2 or 4 GiB VM therefore emitted a limit no device with the claimed memory would emit, contradicting navigator.device-memory - invisible on a developer's large machine and live on the machines this browser is actually run on.
evidence.source: Heap::OldGenerationSizeFromPhysicalMemory and Heap::MaxReserved, reached from IsolateHolder::getDefaultIsolateParams

evidence.note: both readouts go through one MemoryInfo over V8's heap statistics, so a single emitter serves both. WindowPerformance::memory chooses Precision::kPrecise when the process is locked to a site and kBucketized otherwise; MainThreadDebugger::memoryInfo is always kBucketized; the thread-local HeapSizeCache is shared, so a precise read poisons a later bucketized one for twenty minutes.

supplies Profile::memory_total_bytes clamped to the host with std::min, so V8 performs its own arithmetic and capacity is only ever reduced, matching the clamp in patches 0004 and 0006. The reported limit is therefore one the heap genuinely honours rather than an accessor override, which is why it cannot be falsified by allocation.

evidence.note: the CDP input handler seeds every event's modifiers with blink::WebInputEvent::kFromDebugger

CORRECTION. kFromDebugger is bit 23. A whole-tree grep finds no read of it anywhere under third_party/blink - only the browser-side synthetic gesture targets and the input handler itself consume it - and it is not a member of kKeyModifiers (:164-165) or of the four modifiers getModifierState maps, so it never reaches JavaScript. resources/surfaces.json says of Event.isTrusted that events 'dispatched via dispatchEvent or CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent (without untrusted=false) read as false - direct automation tell'. The dispatchEvent half is right; the CDP half is wrong, and the suggested remedy ('real OS-level input injection') is unnecessary.
is_trusted_ is false only for events constructed from script; events built from a WebInputEvent are marked trusted on the normal path, which CDP input takes unmodified

notes: This is the subsystem's clearest instance of the trap in docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md: the T2 row names a value (isTrusted) when the real signal is behavioural. What actually separates driven input from human input is kinematics - pointermove spacing, the dwell between mousedown and mouseup, whether pressure and tiltX vary, whether KeyboardEvent.repeat is ever true across a long key sequence - and none of that is a field Chromium sets wrongly. It is a property of how the driver moves the mouse, so it belongs in user guidance and in whatever input helper Apostate ships, not in a patch. Filed as inherit so the row cannot be mistaken for a to-do.
observable: Event.isTrusted, MouseEvent.getModifierState(...), and navigator.userActivation.{isActive,hasBeenActive} for input synthesised by CDP Input.dispatch*Event
verdict_reason: CDP input is injected into the browser-side input pipeline as a WebInputEvent, the same object real OS input produces, so the resulting DOM events are trusted and carry no JavaScript-visible marker. The only stamp Chromium adds is a WebInputEvent modifier bit that Blink never reads and that is not one of the modifiers getModifierState exposes. There is no value to correct.

evidence.note: THE FINDING. Apply() ends with emulated_screen_info.available_rect = screen_rect, unconditionally, whenever the emulator is active. screen_rect is the emulated screen size if one was given and the real screen rect otherwise, but available_rect is overwritten either way. So ANY Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride collapses the available area onto the full screen - screen.availWidth === screen.width and screen.availHeight === screen.height - regardless of what was requested.
so on a machine claiming macOS the emulated value is not merely different, it is structurally impossible: no macOS desktop has a zero-height menu bar

evidence.note: the window path runs probe::ApplyUserAgentOverride, so Emulation.setUserAgentOverride and Network.setUserAgentOverride reach navigator.userAgent on the main thread

WorkerGlobalScope::UserAgent() returns the stored user_agent_ with no probe. A dedicated worker gets the overridden string only because DedicatedWorker passes execution_context->UserAgent() at construction - a snapshot. A worker created before the override, or re-read after the override changes, disagrees with the window.

THE REFUTATION. A service worker's user_agent is params->user_agent = browser_client->GetUserAgent(), taken in the BROWSER process from the global user agent. No renderer-side inspector probe is in that path at all, so a CDP user-agent override never reaches ServiceWorkerGlobalScope.navigator.userAgent. Fetching a page's own service worker registration and asking it for its UA refutes any CDP-based UA spoof in one call.

note the asymmetry within the worker itself: GetUserAgentMetadata() DOES consult probe::ApplyUserAgentMetadataOverride while UserAgent() does not, so a worker can be made to report userAgentData and userAgent that disagree

notes: The generalisation of the navigator.platform finding, and the strongest single argument in this shard for source patching over CDP. The pattern is not 'CDP misses workers'; it is that each override has its own reach, decided independently by whoever added it, and the reaches disagree: userAgent reaches the window and a dedicated worker created afterwards, userAgentData reaches the window and every worker, and neither reaches a service worker. Any spoof built on Emulation.setUserAgentOverride is refutable by comparing four scopes, and no amount of care in using CDP fixes that, because the missing path is in the browser process. navigator-identity owns the UA value itself (navigator.user-agent); this row owns the constraint that it must be produced somewhere all four scopes read from. V3 should compare all four scopes as an equality assertion.
observable: navigator.userAgent read from the window, from a DedicatedWorker, from a SharedWorker and from a ServiceWorkerGlobalScope, compared for equality

It does NOT work on Windows (uprv_detectWindowsTimeZone), and the environment is readable by anything running in the process, so treat it as a macOS/Linux fast path rather than the design. HAZARD to handle either way: time_zone_monitor_mac.mm:25 re-runs detectHostTimeZone on every NSSystemTimeZoneDidChangeNotification, so a system timezone change mid-session reverts an unpatched detection path.

Verification is therefore V2 rather than V3: the check is that the browser's own belief matches the profile, observed through the value it pushes, not through a fingerprint diff. Because time_zone_monitor.cc:42 drops no-op updates, a patch that sets the browser's ICU default BEFORE the TimeZoneMonitor is constructed is strictly simpler than one that tries to drive the monitor afterwards. WHY THIS ROW MEETS ITS REQUIRED TIER AND STAYS OPEN, since the reconciliation report flags the pair: achieved V2 is the MECHANICAL fact that this patch is inside a series that built green on three platforms and whose artifact launches and passes the smoke suite. This row's required V2 is a SPECIFIC OBSERVATION at that class of check — that the browser process's own icu::TimeZone::createDefault belief matches the profile, observed through the value it pushes rather than through a fingerprint diff — and nobody has made it. The tier label is therefore met while the verification is not, which is a real state and not a bookkeeping error; the row closes when the observation is made, not when the label matches. Decision recorded here rather than by closing the row or suppressing the report line.

evidence.note: adoptDefault writes a single file-static DEFAULT_ZONE under gDefaultZoneMutex - there is no per-thread and no per-isolate ICU default, so a worker in the same process is structurally incapable of holding a different zone from its parent

each isolate's DateCache holds its own ICUTimezoneCache, which clones icu::TimeZone::createDefault() lazily on first use; a worker isolate that never received the flush would keep serving offsets from a stale clone

Clear(kRedetect) would call adoptDefault(detectHostTimeZone()) and revert the process to the host zone; it is unreachable today because DateTimeConfigurationChangeNotification defaults to kSkip (v8/include/v8-isolate.h:1843) and no Chromium caller passes kRedetect

a SharedWorker or ServiceWorker hosted in a SEPARATE renderer process runs its own CoreInitializer and its own TimeZoneController::Init, and receives the browser's push at bind time - so cross-process worker agreement depends entirely on the browser holding the right value

notes: ANSWER TO 'CAN A WORKER'S ICU DEFAULT DIVERGE FROM ITS PARENT'S': not within a process, and the reason is ICU's own design rather than anything Blink does - DEFAULT_ZONE is one file-static. Divergence has exactly two possible shapes. (a) STALE V8 CACHE: the ICU value is global but each isolate caches a clone in its DateCache, so a worker whose isolate missed DateTimeConfigurationChangeNotification reports the old offset while the main thread reports the new one. Blink already closes this with CallOnAllWorkerThreads (timezone_controller.cc:246), and any patch that writes adoptDefault without reproducing that fan-out re-opens it - this is the concrete way a renderer-only timezone patch gets caught by a two-line worker probe. (b) CROSS-PROCESS: a SharedWorker or ServiceWorker in its own renderer gets its zone from the browser's push, so it is correct if and only if browser.icu-default is correct. Both failure modes are eliminated by setting the zone at base/i18n/icu_util.cc InitializeIcuTimeZone, since every process including a dedicated worker host runs it before creating any isolate. CORPUS GAP, and it is actionable: capture/collector/collector.js has 36 probes and none of them reads a Date or an Intl object inside a worker - headers.echo_worker is the only worker probe and it only inspects request headers. Add a worker probe returning {tz, offsetJan, offsetJul, dateToString} so this row can reach V3; today it cannot, which is why corpus_coverage is absent while the surface is one of the most commonly probed in the field. Arbiter: the shard proposed this as spoof with seven emitters, every one correctly marked a waypoint — which is precisely the argument that it is not independently spoofable. The validator caught the contradiction as a spoof verdict with no source of truth.
observable: inside a Worker or SharedWorker: new Date().getTimezoneOffset() and Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, compared against the same two expressions on the main thread
verdict_reason: A worker does not produce a timezone. ICU's default zone is a single file-static per process, so a worker reads the same value the main thread reads and cannot diverge from it except through a stale per-isolate V8 DateCache. There is nothing here to spoof separately; correctness follows from intl.resolved-timezone, and coh.timezone-across-contexts enforces the agreement.

evidence.note: January equals July, so the captured device is in a zone with no DST - which for a UTC+7 zone is a much stronger assertion than the name Asia/Bangkok alone

THE RULE, IN OUR OWN CHECKOUT. Asia/Bangkok is `trans:intvector { -1570084924 }` with `typeOffsets:intvector { 24124, 0, 25200, 0 }` - one transition in 1920 and thereafter raw 25200s with dst 0. That yields exactly -420 in every month of every modern year, reproducing the T0 measurement from a file DEPS pins rather than from anything on the host

ICUTimezoneCache::GetOffsets calls icu::TimeZone::getOffset (UTC input) or BasicTimeZone::getOffsetFromLocal (local input) and LocalTimeOffset returns raw_offset + dst_offset - the JS number is a direct read of the OlsonTimeZone transition table
createSystemTimeZone builds that OlsonTimeZone from openOlsonResource(id), i.e. from zoneinfo64 inside icudtl.dat - the host supplies the zone NAME, our build supplies every offset that name implies
DateCache::GetLocalOffsetFromOS forwards to the ICU cache because icu_timezone_data defaults true; the long non-ICU DST approximation below it is dead in a Chromium build

notes: THE ROW THAT MAKES THE TIMEZONE FREE TO GET RIGHT. Once the zone NAME is correct, every offset a detector can compute follows from icudtl.dat, which is identical on every host running our binary - there is no second value to keep in sync and no way for a per-host difference to creep in. The corollary is the trap: a patch that fakes getTimezoneOffset numerically instead of adopting a zone must reproduce the entire transition table, and the January/July pair in this very probe is the cheapest possible test of whether it did. corpus_coverage is 'present' because the capture holds offsetJan and offsetJul directly, but they are CHECK values, never inputs: the profile stores locale.timezone and ICU derives the offsets, exactly as navigator.device-memory stores real RAM and lets Chromium do the bucketing. Any historical instant is fair game for a detector - new Date(0).getTimezoneOffset() reads the 1970 row of the same table - so replaying a handful of measured offsets cannot work.

notes: The cheapest single expression that tests three of this shard's rows at once, which is why detectors like it: the GMT offset must match the DST rule, the parenthetical must be the right zone's name, and it must be that name rendered in the right locale. Adopting the correct icu::TimeZone gets all three for free because every part is derived. Two specific hazards. First, the parenthetical moves with the ICU LOCALE, not with navigator.language - a profile that changes one without the other produces "Indochina Time" next to a French Accept-Language, or worse, a French zone name next to en-US in Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale. evidence.note: PER-PLATFORM RESOLUTION, settled at T1 and it is three different mechanisms. linux takes GetApplicationLocaleInternalNonMac's USE_GLIB && !IS_CHROMEOS branch and reads g_get_language_names(), i.e. glib's LANGUAGE / LC_ALL / LC_MESSAGES / LANG precedence, without pushing pref_locale as a candidate at all -- so the environment is the whole lever and --lang moves nothing, which is what the stock-Chrome measurement found from outside. macos takes GetApplicationLocaleInternalMac, which uses GetLocaleOverride() first, filled by OverrideLocaleWithCocoaLocale() from OuterBundle().preferredLocalizations in ChromeMainDelegate::PreBrowserMain, and never reads the environment: measured on the shipped macos-arm64 bundle, LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 LANGUAGE=de, LANGUAGE=th LANG=th_TH.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8 each leave Intl at en-US. windows tries pref_locale, then GetLocaleOverrides(), then base::i18n::GetConfiguredLocale() -- ICU's own default, taken from GetUserDefaultLocaleName rather than the environment. Chromium reaches the call from ResourceBundle::LoadLocaleResources, whose GetApplicationLocale() default argument is what calls SetICUDefaultLocale; the browser gets there through PreCreateThreadsImpl -> LoadLocalState -> InitResourceBundleAndDetermineLocale, and a child through ChromeMainDelegate::PreSandboxStartup's SubprocessNeedsResourceBundle block. So macOS leaks the host's system UI language and Windows the host's user default locale, by routes the environment fix does not touch; both are pre-existing and both are this row's remaining escalation.

WRITING THE FOUR VARIABLES IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, which is what fixes the shape of patch 0114. content/app/content_main.cc:255,263 runs setlocale(LC_ALL, "") and setlocale(LC_NUMERIC, "C") before any embedder hook exists, so the C library has already adopted the operator's environment. A glib program running the same calls in the same order on the artifact's own host: with LANG=en_US.UTF-8 inherited, LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 and names[0]=en_US.UTF-8; after writing the composed environment, names[0]=de-DE but LC_MESSAGES is STILL en_US.UTF-8 -- glib reads LANGUAGE live, the C library does not; after setlocale(LC_ALL,"C") and re-adopting, LC_MESSAGES=C with names[0] still de-DE, which is byte-for-byte the state a launcher-set environment produces for a locale the host has not generated. So the fix writes the variables AND re-runs content's two calls from "C", the locale a fresh process starts in. Children need no second decision: LaunchProcess starts from the live environ unless a caller overrides it (launch_posix.cc:308-320), the zygote forks at content_main_runner_impl.cc:1059, where InitializeZygoteSandboxForBrowserProcess "tickles the zygote host so it forks now", against PreSandboxStartup at :1001, and a renderer's --lang is the browser's resolved locale (render_process_host_impl.cc:3781-3783), which is also what blink::DefaultLanguage() and therefore locale-dependent font fallback follow.

evidence.note: WINDOWS: A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER ENTRY. The candidate list is pref_locale, then GetLocaleOverrides(), then base::i18n::GetConfiguredLocale() -- and the last of those is where GetUserDefaultLocaleName enters, which is what this row previously named as the Windows leak. It is not what answers. content_main_runner_impl.cc:1210-1217 calls l10n_util::OverrideLocaleWithUILanguageList() immediately after PreBrowserMain whenever the override is empty, filling it from base::win::i18n::GetThreadPreferredUILanguageList(), so in the browser the second candidate always has a value and the ICU fallback is unreachable. It is reachable only in a process where that call never ran, and a Windows child receives --lang from the browser as pref_locale instead. So the Windows leak is the user's PREFERRED UI LANGUAGE LIST, not the user default locale. Note also that the macOS and Windows override sites are the same shape -- each guarded on `if (override.empty())` with the comment 'Don't do this if the locale is already set' -- so Chromium already has a pinned-locale concept on both.

PATCH 0115 EXECUTED ON THE APPLE BRANCH, which is the check whose absence made an earlier attempt at this surface a compile-clean no-op. Through a throwaway in ui_base_unittests that pointed base::apple::SetOverrideFrameworkBundlePath at the shipped artifact's framework, so the real 220-pak bundle answered CheckAndResolveLocale. Five arms, all with pref_locale=fr so the platform candidate is servable: no --apostate-profile -> fr, i.e. Chromium's own candidates untouched for a launch that is not ours; composed with no locale named -> en-US; --fingerprint-locale=de-DE,de -> de, narrowed by CheckAndResolveLocale because the bundle ships de.lproj and not de_DE, which is Chromium's own region-stripping and matches what the live artifact reports for the same switch; --fingerprint-locale=sw-KE,sw -> sw, same narrowing, because sw.lproj/locale.pak IS shipped -- the expectation that this would fall back was mine and was wrong, the code was right; and --fingerprint-locale=tlh-AA,tlh -> en-US and NOT fr, which is the safety property: an unservable composed locale falls back to the composed default and never through to the host. The committed test covering the same precedence is L10nUtilTest.ApostateComposedLocaleOutranksThePlatformCandidates, which uses tlh rather than a plausible language for exactly the reason the fourth arm shows, and which is excluded on Apple and Android for the reason Chromium's own GetAppLocale test is: on Apple GetLocaleFilePath resolves against the framework bundle's <locale>.lproj and a test binary is not a bundle, so the data cannot be faked through ui::DIR_LOCALES.
