notes: ESCALATED, and the reason is a claim I can prove about the CODE but not yet about the WORLD. What is settled at T1: Intl's locale is the C library's LC_MESSAGES locale as read by ICU, it is entirely independent of the Accept-Language pref that produces navigator.language and the Accept-Language header, and no desktop Chrome code path connects the two. That makes this the fifth confirmed multi-process/multi-source duplication in the project and structurally the same shape as coh.accept-language-header-vs-js - one apparent concept, two unrelated producers. What follows from it, and is the part that needs measuring: on macOS a Finder-launched app inherits no LANG, so setlocale returns "C", ICU returns en_US_POSIX and isolate.cc:8128 rewrites it to "en-US" - meaning stock Chrome on a FRENCH Mac would also report Intl locale "en-US", and a profile that sets Intl locale to fr-FR to match a French Accept-Language would then be WRONG against the real device it claims to be. The same binary started from a terminal with LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 reports fr-FR, so the value also depends on how the operator launched us, which is intolerable on its own. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one capture of stock Chrome on a macOS host whose system language is not English, launched from Finder, reading intl.locale.resolvedOptions.locale alongside navigator.language. If it reports en-US, the correct behaviour is to pin Intl locale to en-US for all macOS profiles and let only navigator.language vary; if it reports fr-FR, macOS must be setting LANG for GUI apps by a route I have not found and locale.icu_locale becomes a real profile field. A second capture on Windows is needed regardless, because uprv_getDefaultLocaleID takes the Win32 branch there and reads GetUserDefaultLocaleName rather than the environment, so the answer is certainly different. RECOMMENDATION FOR EITHER OUTCOME: the launcher must set LANG/LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES explicitly in the browser process environment rather than inheriting the operator's shell. That makes the value deterministic, it is inherited by every child process for free, and it is the same mechanism a real POSIX host uses - no C++ and no A1 exposure. Do NOT patch Isolate::DefaultLocale or SetICUDefaultLocale to force a value: both would leave the C library disagreeing with ICU, which is observable through any code that formats via strftime or reads LANG. ---- MEASURED, and the mechanism half is settled: the recommendation above is CORRECT and implementable, and it does not work on our artifact for a reason that is ours to fix. The lever on Linux is the process environment and NOT --lang. Stock Google Chrome 151, which ships all 220 locale paks: --lang=de-DE and --lang=fr-FR move nothing, while LANGUAGE=de, LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 and LANG=de_DE.UTF-8 each move every family member together -- navigator.languages de-DE,de,en-US,en, navigator.language de-DE, DateTimeFormat/NumberFormat/Collator de, Date 1.1.1970 00:00:00, Number 1.234.567,89. The application locale feeds the Accept-Language default as well as ICU's, so one lever drives both producers, which is what the recommendation was reaching for. The same three variables move nothing on our own artifact, because scripts/package-artifact.sh keeps locales/en-US.pak as the sole pak in the required set for linux-x64, linux-arm64 and windows-x64 (lines 54 and 72), so l10n_util has exactly one UI bundle to resolve against and can only ever answer en-US. Chromium's build produces the full set; packaging discards it. macos-arm64 packages Chromium.app wholesale and already carries 55 .lproj. This is therefore a packaging defect and not a build invariant, and shipping one pak is itself a divergence from stock, which ships them all. The instruction not to patch Isolate::DefaultLocale or SetICUDefaultLocale still holds, and gained a second reason: a call inside InitializeICU is overwritten by the application-locale call that runs after it, so it compiles clean and does nothing -- one such patch was written and withdrawn unbuilt. Do not mix paks across versions to test this: Chromium 153's paks beside our 152 binary core-dump, because resource ids are version-specific. What is still open is the world half, unchanged: whether stock on a non-English-UI host reports its own locale or en-US, which needs a capture on such a host. ---- CLOSED ON LINUX BY PATCH 0114, and the packaging fix is what made it urgent: with 440 paks the lever this row identified became live and nothing in the browser held the other end, so the operator's shell decided a composed persona's Intl locale, Accept-Language default, calendar, hour cycle, collation, number and date formatting, <input type=date> width and CJK font fallback -- measured, all of it, on the new artifact. 0114 writes LANGUAGE, LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES and LANG in the browser process from InstallComposedProfile, the PreSandboxStartup call site patch 0084 established, which is after the compositor and before both the zygote fork and PreCreateThreadsImpl where the locale is resolved. Precedence: an explicit --fingerprint-locale, then the composed default en-US, then the host only under --fingerprint=host. It mirrors the launchers rather than supplying the locale to l10n_util, for the reason this row already gives: forcing the resolution while leaving the C library on the operator's value is the split that is observable through strftime and LANG. The earlier instruction not to patch Isolate::DefaultLocale or SetICUDefaultLocale is untouched and this is not that -- it moves the application locale those calls are given, not the calls. STILL OPEN, unchanged and now the only open half: macOS resolves from NSBundle preferredLocalizations and Windows from GetUserDefaultLocaleName, so neither host's own language is reached by an environment fix, and whether stock Chrome on a non-English-UI host reports its own locale or en-US still decides whether reproducing that is correct or a defect. ---- CLOSED ON macOS AND WINDOWS BY PATCH 0115, which is what the paragraph above called the only open half of the mechanism. 0114 pinned the environment and the environment is the linux lever and only the linux lever; 0115 resolves the composed locale in l10n_util::GetApplicationLocaleInternal, ahead of every platform candidate -- ahead of glib on linux, of NSBundle preferredLocalizations on macOS, and of both --lang and the Windows preferred-UI-language list on windows. One point rather than three platform slots, because pre-filling the macOS and Windows override holders would still sit BELOW windows' pref_locale, where a kApplicationLocale already stored in an existing --user-data-dir's Local State would outrank a composed persona through a persisted channel. One decision too: base::apostate::ComposedApplicationLocale() is what 0114's environment write now reads as well, so the resolution-side pin and the environment-side pin cannot disagree. No C-library split arises, which was this row's standing objection to touching the resolution: on macOS, which is POSIX, 0114 already rewrote the four variables and re-ran setlocale from "C", so the C library is already at the composed locale; on windows nothing ever adopted the environment, because the setlocale(LC_ALL,"") block is IS_POSIX && !IS_ANDROID and base::win::SetupCRT only touches CRT report modes, so the CRT stays in the "C" locale exactly as on stock. --lang becomes inert under a composed profile on all three platforms as a result -- it already was on linux and macOS and said nothing, and on windows it was the first candidate, so that is a real behaviour change -- and it is reported in the explain limitations rather than honoured or refused, which also closes the dead ComposeRequest::accept_languages field 0111 filed as its own defect. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is only the world half, unchanged since the first entry: whether stock Chrome on a host whose system language is not English reports its own locale or en-US. That decides whether a macOS persona reflecting its host's system language would have been a correct reproduction of a real device -- and it no longer decides what this binary should do, because a composed persona serving the operator's own system language is a contradiction against its own navigator.languages either way.

notes: Two separate observables ride this one probe and they need different treatment. The VALUES are a pure function of the resolved locale, so getting intl.resolved-locale right gets them right and nothing else is required - which is why profile_field is locale.icu_locale rather than a field of its own. The KEY SET is a V8-version fingerprint: roundingIncrement, roundingMode, roundingPriority and trailingZeroDisplay only appear once the NumberFormat v3 proposal shipped, so the presence of exactly these fifteen keys dates the engine independently of the UA string. That is a build fact, identical on every host running our binary, and it belongs to coh.icu-data-vs-chromium-version rather than to any device claim. Note the collector records the object in key order, and V8 emits it in a fixed order, so key ORDER is a third free observable that a synthesised object would get wrong.

notes: The resolvedOptions object is the weak half of this surface; the strong half is the COMPARISON FUNCTION, which the collector does not currently probe. Collation order is a large, high-entropy table read out of icudtl.dat, and because that file is DEPS-pinned it is identical on every host running our build - so like intl.supported-values it is free to get right and impossible to get wrong per-host, and it can only be wrong if we claim a locale whose collation differs from the one we actually loaded. Worth adding a sort-order probe to the collector for exactly the same reason the font shard wants queryLocalFonts: it converts a cheap key/value comparison into a wide one at no cost.

evidence.note: the retained M4 capture reports 418 time zones and 18 calendars; ICU data is build-pinned as described by the source evidence below

THE ARITHMETIC, DONE AGAINST OUR OWN CHECKOUT. The typeMap holds 447 canonical zone entries. Of those, 29 are Etc/* (Etc/GMT, Etc/GMT+1..+12, Etc/GMT-1..-14, Etc/UTC, Etc/Unknown). 447 - 29 = 418, which is the measured value exactly

and the filter that produces that subtraction: TZEnumeration excludes Etc/Unknown by name (:643), excludes every id whose ZoneMeta::getCanonicalCLDRID differs from itself i.e. every alias (:647-656), and excludes every id whose region is "001" (:658-666), which is precisely the 28 remaining Etc entries
Intl::AvailableCalendars passes icu::Locale("und") explicitly, so the 18-entry calendar list is locale-independent as well as host-independent
the data these lists come from is TZVersion 2025c inside ICU 78.2, both fixed by DEPS:2364 icu@d578f2e8b7bd5938e21cfb6bf15c079e0aa5b738

notes: THE ANSWER TO QUESTION (a), and it is the good kind of answer. ICU's timezone and locale data is NOT read from the host: base/i18n/icu_util.cc:174 resolves icudtl.dat inside our own framework bundle, :248 hands the mmapped bytes to udata_setCommonData, and :280 then calls udata_setFileAccess(UDATA_ONLY_PACKAGES) with the comment "Never try to load ICU data from files", after which ICU is structurally unable to read host tz or locale data at all. The file is checked in at third_party/icu/common/icudtl.dat and pinned by DEPS. Consequently the full supportedValuesOf('timeZone') list, the calendar list, every DST rule and the whole collation table are properties of OUR BUILD, byte-identical on every host that runs it - free to get right, impossible to get wrong per-host. The 418/447-29 derivation above is the proof: a measured value reproduced from source with no host term in it. This is the counterpart to the ANGLE and audio findings but with the opposite sign - there the value turned out to be a build fact we could not control per-host, here it is a build fact we do not need to. The ONE way to break it is to ship an ICU that disagrees with the Chrome milestone we claim, since Chrome 152 shipped ICU 78.2/tz2025c and a fork that rolled ICU independently would emit a count no real Chrome 152 emits. Recorded as coh.icu-data-vs-chromium-version. Second-order note for the timezone rows: because the enumeration excludes aliases, a zone id that is an alias (Asia/Calcutta, US/Pacific) is not in this list even though it is a valid argument to createTimeZone - see coh.resolved-timezone-in-supported-set.

verdict_reason: The lists are computed entirely from the DEPS-pinned icudtl.dat with no host input on any code path, so our build already emits exactly what stock Chrome of the same milestone emits. There is nothing per-host to spoof and no profile field could improve it; the only way to get it wrong is to ship a different ICU than the Chrome version we claim, which coh.icu-data-vs-chromium-version covers.

evidence.note: fourteen of the twenty are one-line forwards to LIBC_NAMESPACE::shared::<fn> from #include "third_party/llvm-libc/src/shared/math.h" - in-tree source pinned by DEPS:534 llvm_libc_revision 3ea89f4304312567e31a8eb45e0737577e65b676, compiled into our binary. The host libm is not linked into any of them

and they are correctly rounded, not merely deterministic: a Ziv rounding test falls through to an accurate pass when the fast path is inconclusive, LIBC_MATH_HAS_SKIP_ACCURATE_PASS is defined nowhere in the build, and the FMA use is gated on compile-time predefines (__ARM_FEATURE_FMA, __AVX2__ && __FMA__) with no runtime CPUID dispatch. So unlike the rustfft kernels these results cannot vary with the host CPU

acosh, asinh, atanh, cosh and sinh remain hand-ported fdlibm, but they are composed out of the llvm-libc primitives plus sqrt and fabs - and sqrt lowers to the hardware square-root instruction, which IEEE-754 requires to be correctly rounded. Five more build constants
THE EXCEPTION. `double tanh(double x) { return std::tanh(x); }` - the one function in the file still calling <cmath>, so Math.tanh is Apple libm on macOS, glibc on Linux and UCRT on Windows

THE SECOND EXCEPTION, and the less visible one. math::pow returns std::pow(x,y) whenever v8_flags.use_std_math_pow, and that flag is DEFINE_BOOL(..., true) everywhere except AIX. V8's own llvm-libc pow at v8/src/base/ieee754.cc:300 is dead code on all our targets
every JIT tier constant-folds through the same base::ieee754 and i::math::pow entry points, so a value does not change when a function tiers up - A3 holds within a session by construction

notes: THE ANSWER TO QUESTION (b), and it is a split rather than a verdict. Eighteen of the twenty probed values are BUILD facts: fourteen are llvm-libc forwards from source pinned in our own checkout, five more (acosh, asinh, atanh, cosh, sinh) are fdlibm compositions over those same primitives, and sqrt is the hardware instruction. Better than merely build-determined, the llvm-libc doubles are CORRECTLY ROUNDED behind a Ziv test with an accurate fallback and their only FMA gating is compile-time, so they do not vary with the host CPU the way the audio shard's rustfft kernels do - the same binary gives the same bits on any arm64 or x86-64 host, and an arm64 build and an x86-64 build agree with each other too. TWO ARE HOST FACTS. Math.tanh is std::tanh at v8/src/base/ieee754.cc:361, the single line in that file still bound to <cmath>. Math.pow is std::pow, because use_std_math_pow defaults true (flag-definitions.h:1232) and V8's own pow is dead - which is the more dangerous of the two, since Math.pow appears in more fingerprinting scripts than any other transcendental. Both bind to Apple libm here, glibc on Linux, UCRT on Windows. So the shape is the mirror image of the audio finding: there almost everything was host- or CPU-determined and only the framing was build-determined; here almost everything is build-determined and exactly two functions leak the OS. WHAT IS UNRESOLVED, and what would settle it: whether Apple libm, glibc and UCRT actually DISAGREE at the two probed arguments, tanh(1) and pow(PI,-100). Both are plausibly correctly rounded in all three, in which case the leak is theoretical and this row closes as inherit. Needed: the same two expressions evaluated on (a) a glibc Linux x86-64 host, (b) a Windows/UCRT host, (c) an arm64 Linux host - three numbers, obtainable in minutes from any Chrome, no capture pipeline required. RECOMMENDATION IF THEY DIFFER, in preference order. (1) Set --use_std_math_pow=false, which is an existing in-tree V8 flag that routes Math.pow back to base::ieee754::legacy::pow, i.e. llvm-libc, i.e. our build - this converts pow from a host fact to a build fact with a one-word change and no patch, and it is the AIX configuration so it is a supported path rather than a hack. Verify first that the llvm-libc answer matches what real Chrome on the CLAIMED os emits, because on macOS real Chrome emits the Apple libm answer and matching our own build would then be the wrong target. (2) For tanh, replace std::tanh at ieee754.cc:361 with the llvm-libc shared tanh if one exists at the pinned revision, or with the fdlibm composition over expm1 that the neighbouring sinh/cosh already use - a self-contained change to one line. (3) If either function must stay host-bound, partition profiles by OS family exactly as the audio shard partitions by (os-family, cpu-isa-class), and refuse a macOS profile on a Linux host. Explicitly rejected: perturbing the returned doubles, which is A3 per-call noise wearing a different hat and is caught by a single corpus diff.
observable: Math.{acos,acosh,asin,asinh,atan,atanh,cbrt,cos,cosh,exp,expm1,log,log1p,log10,sin,sinh,sqrt,tan,tanh}(x) at fixed arguments, plus Math.pow(Math.PI,-100). The full-precision doubles, usually concatenated and hashed.

evidence.note: CanWebpageContextConnectExternally iterates the renderer's main-thread extension set and returns true on the first externally_connectable manifest whose matches cover the context URL. That answer alone installs the runtime accessor and sets the browser object on a web page, so one boolean reproduces the whole gate and no extension has to be named.

Everything behind the gate is already the real binding path: the feature file grants runtime.connect and runtime.sendMessage to web_page over <all_urls>, the hooks delegate installs id and dynamicId as undefined-returning native data properties, and a web-page channel to any extension id - absent, present, or present but not connectable - is answered with the identical kReceivingEndDoesntExistError, deliberately, so widening the gate creates no enumeration oracle.

Presence is an ordinary state for a large real population - MetaMask alone has tens of millions of installs - and the shape is the same across wallet and automation extensions. RabbyHub/Rabby ships externally_connectable ids [] and therefore has no web-page runtime, so the population genuinely splits. The Hangouts and Gemini component extensions are official-build-only and match Google properties, which is why a Chromium fork sees absence on a fresh profile.
evidence.source: MetaMask/metamask-extension app/manifest/v3/chrome.json; AmbireTech/extension; ethereum/kohaku-extension; chrome/common/features.gni:61 with chrome/browser/extensions/component_loader.cc

evidence.note: The browser-side re-check is untouched by the series, so widening the renderer gate does not change what a real installed extension receives: OpenChannelToExtension re-checks the target's externally_connectable in the browser process against util::GetURLForExtensionPermissionCheck(source_render_frame_host) and returns kReceivingEndDoesntExistError on failure, with the in-tree comment that the identical error exists so nothing leaks about the extension. A page on a composed identity therefore gets the same answer for an id that does not exist, one that exists and declared another URL, and one that declared nothing. extension_frame_host.cc forwards the mojo call unconditionally and has no ReceivedBadMessage on the path, so a renderer that asks more often cannot be killed for it.

evidence.note: Assertion driver at /tmp/w2/ChromeRuntimeGate/probe.js: two launches with a fresh --user-data-dir and no extension installed, one per seed, each visiting https://example.com/ and a local file:// page. On this host the extensions axis draws externally-connectable for --fingerprint=4 and absent for --fingerprint=1 (11 of seeds 1..59 draw present, the 75/25 table on a small sample); the seeds were found with scripts/profile_resolver.py, which reproduces this binary's every other axis choice for both seeds exactly. Run against the shipped pre-patch binary, 12 of its 26 assertions hold and they are precisely the bare ones -- both URLs on the absent seed and file:// on the present seed, chrome own keys ['loadTimes','csi','app'], chrome.runtime and window.browser undefined, no own 'browser' on window -- and all 14 present-and-https assertions fail. That is the surface 0121 adds, so the driver is known to fail before it is trusted to pass; this wave does not build, so the present state is an expectation and the patch body carries it field by field.

notes: SERVED as of 0121. 0116 composed the axis and left it with no caller; 0121 is the caller and is one predicate in CanWebpageContextConnectExternally -- return true additionally when the profile carries extensions.externally_connectable true and the context URL scheme is http or https, mirroring MetaMask's matches so file:// and about:blank stay bare. Everything downstream is the unmodified binding path, which is why the observable is the pair (chrome.runtime plus window.browser with browser.runtime === chrome.runtime) and not chrome.runtime alone, a state only the Web Store produces. The predicate is ADDITIVE: nullopt falls through, which is --fingerprint=host, and an explicit false also falls through rather than suppressing a real installed extension's match. 0116's row argued the explicit false keeps the host from answering for the persona, and for the default case -- a user-data-dir with no extensions -- an additive gate serves exactly the drawn state. Where they differ is a user-data-dir that really carries a wallet, and there suppression is worse: the page already sees that extension's content script and injected objects, so withdrawing only the runtime accessor composes a state no install produces, and the browser process honours the manifest either way. What must NOT be done instead is shipping an inert component extension to produce the observable: a fixed extension id is a cross-instance correlator that survives every other axis.

evidence.note: Windows. The tuple starts with antialiasing and subpixel positioning off and turns both on when SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHING reports smoothing enabled, which is the default; the subpixel order comes from GetSubpixelRenderingGeometry (ClearType PixelStructure 1 or FE_FONTSMOOTHINGORIENTATIONRGB -> rgb) and is reached only when SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGTYPE is FE_FONTSMOOTHINGCLEARTYPE, also the default. autohinter false, use_bitmaps false and HINTING_MEDIUM are set outright.

macOS states the whole tuple as 'params that match SkiaTextRenderer's default render settings': antialiasing, subpixel positioning, embedded bitmaps and rgb on, autohinter off, HINTING_MEDIUM. use_bitmaps true is macOS alone among the three.

Linux is the leak: the tuple is the toolkit's and then fontconfig's answer, so under a composed persona it is the HOST's desktop configuration. autohinter, use_bitmaps and HINTING_SLIGHT are what Chromium's own FreeType path calls the system default; hintslight is what GTK reports and what FC_HINT_SLIGHT maps to; rgb is fontconfig's rgba on an ordinary LCD desktop; subpixel_positioning is false because it is set to device_scale_factor > 1.0f and an unscaled desktop is 1.0.

text_contrast and text_gamma are per-build Skia defines rather than OS queries, so the coherent value is what a real Chrome on the claimed OS was compiled with: is_win SK_GAMMA_SRGB with contrast 1.0, is_mac SK_GAMMA_SRGB with 0.0, linux exponent 1.2 with contrast 0.2, and SK_GAMMA_SRGB leaves SK_GAMMA_EXPONENT at the header's 0.0f, sRGB. skia_config is an all_dependent_configs of //skia, so ui/gfx and Blink see those defines. The 0.5 fallback in SkTypes.h is for a build defining neither macro and is no desktop Chrome's value. SkSurfaceProps declares the domain the schema and the loader enforce, and font_util_win.cc clamps a registry value into exactly it.

The eight fields cross to the renderer as preferences, so they are settable from a profile without patching any rasteriser -- but four guards stood between the preference and Skia, and 0122 removed or gated all four. UpdateFontRenderingFromRendererPrefs was !IS_MAC in its entirety; text_contrast and text_gamma were [EnableIf=is_win] on the wire and IS_WIN in the browser-side copy; and LegacyDisplayGlobals::SetCachedParams accepted both floats and then stored them under IS_WIN. What remains is not reachable by any setting: the glyph masks are produced by the host's scaler, CoreText on a Mac and FreeType on Linux, and DirectWrite's are not available on either.

The leak, measured on the shipped macos-arm64 build before 0122. --fingerprint=0122 with --fingerprint-platform=windows and =macos, a canvas drawn with fillText in Helvetica, Georgia and Arial -- three families whose advances both personas resolve identically on that host, so the glyph origins match and only rasterisation settings can move a pixel -- returned ONE digest, df91c47fa322e806, under both personas, opaque and alpha, byte-identical across two launches each. Beside it an oracle: -webkit-font-smoothing:none moved the canvas under BOTH personas (8f0a134cb22ebc47 -> b8a9d3c00769b14a), and that property reaches the SkFont on macOS alone -- font_platform_data_win.cc and the generic font_platform_data.cc both leave the FontDescription parameter unnamed -- so a page could read the host platform through it under a Windows persona. Advances were identical across personas and are the baseline the served build must reproduce: 16px Helvetica 177.9296875, 28px Georgia 252.08203125, 13.5px Arial 134.347412109375.
evidence.source: own measurement on the shipped macos-arm64 build; the probe, its page and the expected post-build outcomes are recorded in patches/0122-fonts-render-params-follow-the-persona.patch

evidence.note: Post-build, macos-arm64 carrying 0122, three personas at seed 0122, two launches each, metric-stable canvas of Helvetica/Georgia/Arial at named baselines. windows and macos both df91c47fa322e806, which is the PRE-patch digest; linux f02d5c18b74b2222, and its advances go integral (180 / 241 / 142 against 177.9296875 / 252.08203125 / 134.347412109375). So the chain profile -> gfx::ComposedFontRenderParams -> blink::RendererPreferences -> FontPlatformData::CreateSkFont -> SkFont::setSubpixel is live on a Mac, and the reason windows and macos cannot be told apart there is that their tuples differ in exactly two fields neither of which reaches a glyph on that host: text_contrast, which Skia's CoreText typeface discards, and use_bitmaps, which needs a face with an embedded strike. The -webkit-font-smoothing oracle now reads on == off under the windows and linux personas and on != off under macos. Every advance, ink box, font bounding box and client rect identical to the pre-patch recording for windows and macos. 22 of 22 probe checks pass. A Linux host is unmeasured.

evidence.note: Why four of the eight fields are inert on a Mac, from Skia rather than from inference. SkTypeface_Mac::onFilterRec calls rec->ignorePreBlend() for an unhinted A8 mask unless SK_GAMMA_APPLY_TO_A8 is defined, which skia/BUILD.gn defines for Android alone, and every other branch ends in rec->setContrast(0) commented 'CoreGraphics dialates smoothed text to provide contrast'; the same function collapses hinting to kNormal or kNone and strips kForceAutohinting_Flag in flagsWeDontSupport. Since Apple removed subpixel antialiasing SkCTFontGetSmoothBehavior() is none, which forces hinting kNone and mask format A8, so the ignorePreBlend branch is the live one. Confirmed independently of any Apostate code: --text-contrast and --text-gamma, which render_process_host_impl.cc copies to the renderer and which override at GetSkSurfaceProps time, move no canvas pixel at any value from 0 to 3.9, under GPU raster and under --disable-gpu, while --disable-gpu itself changes the digest. On Linux the equivalent branch keeps the pre-blend whenever LCD text is on, so all four are live there.

notes: SERVED IN EVERY PROCESS AT 0122. 0117 added the schema section, the loader parse, Profile::font_render_params() and the compositor's per-persona projection, and nothing consumed it; 0122 is the consumer. One override -- gfx::ComposedFontRenderParams(), which the macOS, Linux and Windows implementations of GetFontRenderParams each defer to -- so the browser (skia::LegacyDisplayGlobals and viz::GpuHostImpl::InitFontRenderParams from BrowserMainLoop::PreMainMessageLoopRun), the GPU process and every renderer (blink::RendererPreferences) agree without a second delivery path for the same eight numbers. content/browser/browser_main_loop.cc is unchanged for exactly that reason. Four upstream gates went with it, each an IS_WIN or !IS_MAC that was correct while only Windows could produce a contrast or gamma other than the build constant: the content-side copy, the mojom field plus its traits, skia::LegacyDisplayGlobals::SetCachedParams -- which took both floats and stored them under IS_WIN, and would have made the other three look like they worked -- and WebViewImpl::UpdateFontRenderingFromRendererPrefs. chrome/browser/renderer_preferences_util.cc's macOS refresh is gated on the profile rather than made unconditional, so a stock Mac launch still moves no byte. Projected from the persona rather than drawn, and that is the surface rather than a simplification: Chromium has exactly one answer per platform and a tuple mixing two platforms' answers is a machine that does not exist, so --fingerprint-explain reports it on a platform-projection layer with no option count. All eight fields or none, enforced in the loader, because a partial tuple leaves the rest to the host and on Linux 'the rest' is the host's fontconfig. MEASURED ON A MAC HOST AT V2: the chain is live end to end, proved by the linux persona, whose subpixel_positioning false moves the canvas digest and makes advances integral. RESIDUAL, and it is larger than 0117 assumed: four of the eight fields are inert on a Mac because Skia's CoreText typeface discards them -- text_contrast and text_gamma through ignorePreBlend/setContrast(0), hinting collapsed to kNormal-or-kNone, autohinter stripped in flagsWeDontSupport -- so a Windows persona's canvas text on a Mac is byte-identical to a Mac's, which is METHODOLOGY section 9's Mode A measured rather than assumed. All four are live on a Linux host, which is the deployment target and where the leak was worst. And the glyph masks stay the host scaler's. These are the SkFont flags a Windows Chrome sets; the coverage bytes underneath come from CoreText on a Mac and from FreeType on Linux, and DirectWrite's are unreachable from either under any setting. Hinting is inert on a CoreText-backed typeface, so three of the four macOS SkFont settings are observable on a Mac host. -webkit-font-smoothing is honoured on that path only when the persona is macOS, because it changes no glyph byte on Windows or Linux. docs/LIMITATIONS.md 'Text rendering follows the persona' carries all of it. corpus_coverage is absent because no capture field holds the tuple; what a capture holds is its consequence, and those are canvas.2d, fonts.text-advances and canvas.measure-text, which is where a V3 diff would see this move.
observable: Not directly readable. Observable through its consequences: canvas 2D text pixel bytes after getImageData or toDataURL, measureText advances and their fractional part, and client rects of text runs.
